papers.title: Bench note
lines: Three hundred brooches to finish by Friday. Pins in the left tin, springs in the right tin, tea in the cracked cup.
The cat is not to sit on the gold leaf. She knows this. She does it anyway.

papers.title: Pattern card
lines: A lace pattern of oak leaves and acorns, punched on card for the Leavers loom.
In the margin: 'Do not let Brian near this. He has opinions about acorns.'

trail.clue: The pattern-maker's acorn is buried near the hedge. Dig where it would sit.

papers.title: Airman's letter
lines: Dear Mam, we go tonight. Do not worry. The cook has promised bacon on our return.
If I do not write for a while it is because the post is slow. It is not because anything has happened. Love, Ron.

papers.title: Wool merchant's will
lines: I leave my best fleece to the church, my second best to my brother, and my third to the first man who tells me my wool is overpriced.
Witnessed this day by the vicar and a very large sheep.

trail.clue: A merchant's strongbox lies where wool was once weighed, near the old oak.

papers.title: Potter's mark sheet
lines: Fired this week: sixty-two plates, one gravy boat, a teapot with an opinion.
The teapot came out of the kiln with a crack the shape of Wales. We are calling it the Welsh teapot and selling it at a premium.

papers.title: Ironmaster's receipt
lines: For the iron to build the bridge over the Severn, an odd and daring thing.
The old men say iron will sink. The young men say it will float. The river has not yet been consulted.

papers.title: Pencilled directions
lines: Take the Northern line to the stop with the funny name. Change at the one with the stairs.
Do NOT stand on the left. Do not speak to anyone. If a man in a bowler says hello, he is probably lost too.
